old_caption: The video captures a serene view of a waterfront cityscape under a partly cloudy sky. The water is calm, with gentle ripples reflecting the sunlight, and the camera appears to be positioned on a moving boat, as evidenced by the slight wake trailing behind it. In the distance, a bridge spans across the water, connecting two parts of the city. On the right side of the frame, a row of buildings lines the shore, featuring a mix of modern and traditional architecture, with some structures displaying distinct European-style facades. The sky above is a vibrant blue, dotted with fluffy white clouds, adding to the tranquil atmosphere. As the video progresses, there are no significant changes in the scenery or the position of the camera, maintaining a steady focus on the picturesque urban landscape and the expansive waterway.

caption: The video captures a daytime waterfront cityscape viewed from the water, with a low two-towered bridge on the left, a long dark pier across the middle distance, and a hillside skyline crowned by a conical-roofed tower on the right. A blue sky scattered with white cumulus clouds fills the upper half, while dark greenish-blue, choppy water fills the lower half. In the immediate foreground, patches of white foam churn and reshape, wave crests and troughs shifting continuously, showing the viewpoint moving relative to the water. The distant bridge, pier, and skyline remain essentially locked in place, with only negligible apparent drift, so no large pan or zoom is evident. Light-colored boats moored along the right-hand quay show no movement against the shore, and the cloud field stays largely fixed. The sequence reads as one continuous shot of an ongoing process, with the foreground wake actively developing while the broader scene holds steady.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
